newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Japanese hand over $33 million port to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Japanese hand over $33 million port to Cambodia.

text.p: The government of Japan on Saturday announced it had completed $32.7 million in renovations at the Phnom Penh port and handed over the site to Cambodia.
Officials at the handing-over ceremony said it would be a premier port on the Mekong River, allowing 3,000-tonne ships access to the Cambodian capital.
Japanese Ambassador Shohei Naito said the four-year port rehabilitation was an "indispensable tool for the reconstruction of Cambodia".
The new port will be able to handle 570,000 tonnes of cargo a year, said Tram Iv Tek, secretary of state for public works and transport.
Before renovations, the port was handling about 170,000 tonnes annually.
The Japanese government provided new berths, a container yard, lighting for night operations, cranes and forklifts, Tram Iv Tek said.
The original port was constructed in the 1950s. It had fallen into disrepair after decades of civil war, he said.
